extracted.intended_audience: Postal Service customers, mailers, industry stakeholders, and members of the public invited to comment on USPS rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for submitting public comments and the proposed substantive changes to the Domestic Mail Manual (DMM) regarding use of foreign return addresses on domestic mailpieces. Includes submission instructions, deadlines, proposed DMM text, and related operational/claims consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments on or before December 6, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document displays 'Comments Close 12/06/2023' and later notes 'Comments are no longer being accepted.' Submit by the stated date to be considered; late comments will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit comments (mail and email requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mail or deliver written comments to the Director, Product Classification, U.S. Postal Service, 475 L'Enfant Plaza SW, Room 4446, Washington, DC 20260-5015. If sending comments by email, include the name and address of the commenter and send to PCFederalRegister@usps.gov, with a subject line of 'Use of Foreign Return Addresses'. Faxed comments are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When emailing, include the submitter's name and address in the body of the message (not just attachment) and use the specified subject line. Fax submissions will be rejected. Follow address and format directions to ensure the comment is received and properly associated with the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public record / confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: All submitted comments and attachments are part of the public record and subject to disclosure. Do not enclose any material in your comments that you consider to be confidential or inappropriate for public disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume comments and attachments will be publicly viewable and potentially disclosed; do not send sensitive personal or proprietary information unless you understand it will be public. The notice explicitly warns against including confidential material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection and copying of submitted comments
rubrics_metrics.description: You may inspect and photocopy all written comments, by appointment only, at USPS Headquarters Library, 475 L'Enfant Plaza SW, 11th Floor North, Washington, DC 20260. These records are available for review on Monday through Friday, 9 a.m.-4 p.m., by calling 202-268-2906.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments are archived and available for public inspection during stated hours by appointment; include phone number to schedule. Use these procedures to verify what was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy: Use of foreign return addresses on domestic mailpieces (proposed DMM text)
rubrics_metrics.description: When U.S. postage is applied to a domestic mailpiece, as defined under 608.2.1 and 608.2.2, only a domestic return address is authorized. An undeliverable domestic mailpiece bearing a foreign return address cannot be returned to sender and will be handled as dead mail under 507.1.9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the proposed revised text for DMM subsection 602.1.5.4. It eliminates prior courtesy exception allowing a foreign return address on a domestic-piece with U.S. postage and clarifies that undeliverable pieces with foreign return addresses will not be returned internationally but processed as dead mail. The change is proposed to be implemented effective January 1, 2024 if adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indemnity nonpayable condition for certain undeliverable mail
rubrics_metrics.description: Add new nonpayable claim item: 'ag. An undeliverable, registered or insured domestic mailpiece bearing a foreign return address.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under revised DMM 609.4.3 (4.3 Nonpayable Claims), indemnity will not be paid for insured/registered domestic mailpieces that are undeliverable because they bear a foreign return address. This specifies a claims-exclusion consequence of the proposed addressing rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related amendments to other postal manuals/sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Postal Service would also revise related sections of the International Mail Manual (IMM) including subsection 762.2, 'Undeliverable Domestic Mail Bearing U.S. Postage and a Foreign Return Address.' Also revises various other DMM subsections (e.g., 602.1.5.4 and 609.4.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal affects both domestic (DMM) and international (IMM) procedures; reviewers and commenters should consider cross-manual operational impacts and related procedure changes. If adopted, an amendment to 39 CFR part 111 will be published to reflect these changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational/legal justification for the change
rubrics_metrics.description: The Postal Service is authorized pursuant to 39 U.S.C. 404(a)(1) to provide for the disposition of undeliverable mail. However, for the Postal Service to incur destination country delivery charges as a result of attempting to return certain undeliverable domestic mailpieces with a foreign return address is not practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice explains the practical and legal rationale: returning certain pieces internationally would impose impracticable costs, so the policy shifts disposition to dead mail procedures. Commenters may address the reasonableness of this justification and costs/impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date / implementation timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Postal Service is proposing to implement this change effective January 1, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed effective date gives stakeholders a target for operational compliance and transition; if rule adopted, the effective date governs when mailers must use only domestic return addresses on domestic mail bearing U.S. postage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information for further information
rubrics_metrics.description: For further information contact Catherine Knox at (202) 268-5636, Treishawna Harris at (202) 268-2965, or Garry Rodriguez at (202) 268-7281.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these contacts for technical or procedural questions about the proposal prior to submitting comments or to obtain clarifications about the DMM and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication / official format notice
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays a prototype of a 'Web 2.0' version of the daily Federal Register. It is not an official legal edition of the Federal Register. Use the PDF linked in the document sidebar for the official electronic format. Only official editions provide legal notice under 44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing comments or citing the rule, refer to and verify the official PDF on govinfo.gov; do not rely solely on the prototype display for legal research or formal citation.
